title: Butternut Squash and Sage Pasta
subtitle: Roasted squash pasta with crispy sage and pine nuts
excerpt: Roasted butternut squash tossed through pasta with browned butter, crispy sage, and toasted pine nuts. The squash melts into the butter to coat the pasta lightly.
sourceNotes: Northern Italian approach combining roasted squash with browned butter and sage. A classic autumn pasta combination.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the squash up to 2 hours ahead and reheat in the pan with the butter.

content.text: Let the squash get properly caramelised in the oven. Pale roasted squash has very little flavour.

items.prepNote: finely grated, plus extra to serve

content.text: Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Toss the squash with a tablespoon of the butter, melted. Season and spread on a roasting tin. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and tender.
Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
Melt the remaining butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the sage leaves. Fry for 1 to 2 minutes until crispy. Remove the sage and set aside.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes to the butter. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the roasted squash. Mash half of it roughly into the butter to form a loose sauce.
Add the drained pasta and a splash of pasta water. Toss to coat.
Stir in the parmesan. Top with crispy sage and pine nuts. Serve with extra parmesan.

items.symptom: Squash is mushy and has no colour.
items.cause: Pieces were crowded in the tin or oven was not hot enough.
items.fix: Spread into a single layer with space between each piece.

items.cause: Butter too hot or left too long in the pan.
items.fix: Fry sage in medium heat and remove the moment it is crisp.

items.cause: Not enough pasta water or squash absorbed the butter.
items.fix: Add more pasta water a splash at a time until it coats the pasta.
